stance: Structural overweight, but split between direct AI-cooling beta and lower-beta water infrastructure.
themeRead: The data-centre bottleneck is broadening from electricity into heat rejection, liquid cooling, water sourcing, reclaimed-water infrastructure and permitting. The strongest investment setup is not simply 'water demand rises'; it is owning technologies that let data centres secure capacity while using less potable water and less power.

tracked.name: Ecolab
tracked.whatChanged: Ecolab closed the CoolIT acquisition for about $4.75bn. CoolIT year-to-date sales were growing more than 100%, while Ecolab's Q2 organic sales grew 5%, Global High-Tech remained a double-digit growth engine and 2026 EPS guidance was raised.
tracked.bullCase: Uniquely combines ultrapure/process water, power-generation water systems and direct-to-chip liquid cooling. This is valuable if AI infrastructure increasingly needs an integrated water-and-thermal solution rather than separate vendors.
tracked.risk: Premium valuation and integration risk. CoolIT growth is currently extremely high and should not be extrapolated indefinitely.

tracked.name: Modine
tracked.view: Best direct growth play, but execution-sensitive
tracked.whatChanged: Fiscal Q1 2027 sales grew 28%; Data Centers revenue grew 90%; backlog nearly doubled year over year after three consecutive quarters of record orders. Management kept FY2027 guidance of 20%-35% sales growth and $650m-$680m adjusted EBITDA, while acknowledging near-term supply-chain bottlenecks.
tracked.bullCase: The $4bn long-term capacity agreement through 2029, strong data-centre growth and planned portfolio separation make MOD one of the cleanest listed cooling beneficiaries.
tracked.risk: Customer concentration, capacity-expansion execution, supply-chain bottlenecks and temporary margin pressure. This is the sleeve's highest operating-beta name.

tracked.name: Xylem
tracked.whatChanged: Q2 orders reached $3.1bn, up 42% reported and 41% organically, while revenue grew only 2%. Management said water is becoming increasingly strategic to both utilities and industrial customers.
tracked.bullCase: The cleanest broad play on water scarcity, reuse, metering and utility infrastructure. AI/data-centre demand strengthens the long-run case without making the thesis dependent on one cooling architecture.
tracked.risk: Large order growth must convert into revenue and cash flow. Public-project timing and premium infrastructure valuation can create long holding periods.

tracked.name: Vertiv
tracked.whatChanged: Vertiv is expanding chiller manufacturing capacity in Italy, acquired Strategic Thermal Labs and ThermoKey, and recently demonstrated a data-centre cooling retrofit that cut power use by about 20% while eliminating cooling-related water consumption.
tracked.bullCase: One of the most complete AI infrastructure stacks spanning power and cooling. Waterless or very-low-water cooling becomes more valuable where local water constraints delay projects.
tracked.risk: High AI-capex sensitivity and premium valuation; not a pure water stock.

newResearchCandidates.name: Trane Technologies
newResearchCandidates.reason: Q2 organic bookings rose 37%, Americas Commercial HVAC bookings rose 50%, applied-equipment bookings rose 130% and backlog reached a record $12.1bn, up 70%. Trane is also expanding data-centre-specific chillers in Asia-Pacific and agreed to acquire LiquidStack, giving it a path toward end-to-end thermal management.
newResearchCandidates.whatWouldPromote: Confirm valuation is not fully discounting the backlog and that LiquidStack/data-centre revenue becomes material without eroding margins.

newResearchCandidates.name: Veolia Environnement
newResearchCandidates.role: Reclaimed water + water technology + energy/resource integration
newResearchCandidates.reason: Veolia launched Data Center Resource 360 in August and is already working with Amazon on reclaimed-water cooling. It targets more than EUR1bn of annual revenue from data centres and chip production by 2030. H1 EBITDA grew 5% and current net income 10.4%, while management explicitly cited AI-industry resource demand as a structural driver.
newResearchCandidates.whatWouldPromote: Quantify how much of the data-centre pipeline is contracted, margins on the integrated offering, and whether Water Technologies project softness masks improving recurring demand.

newResearchCandidates.name: Veralto
newResearchCandidates.role: Water quality + treatment instrumentation + UV treatment
newResearchCandidates.reason: A lower-hype water-quality picks-and-shovels candidate. Veralto expanded its UV water-treatment portfolio with Alfaa UV in July, strengthening industrial water exposure without relying on AI cooling as the core thesis.
newResearchCandidates.whatWouldPromote: Need a stronger link between recurring water-quality growth and data-centre/semiconductor demand, plus a valuation comparison against XYL and ECL.

currentThemeNews.headline: US data-centre construction is spilling into cooling and industrial supply chains
currentThemeNews.implication: The AI trade is broadening from chips into physical factory capacity and thermal infrastructure; this supports MOD, VRT and TT, but also increases overbuild risk if hyperscaler capex rolls over.

currentThemeNews.headline: Pennsylvania tightens environmental and community rules for new AI data centres
currentThemeNews.implication: Permitting and local acceptance are becoming investment constraints. Efficient cooling and water-reuse systems can become enabling infrastructure rather than optional sustainability spending.

currentThemeNews.headline: OpenAI-linked Australian project drops reclaimed-water plan and switches to waterless cooling
currentThemeNews.implication: This is an important warning against a simplistic 'AI equals more water demand' thesis. Water infrastructure constraints can force projects toward more energy-intensive waterless cooling, benefiting thermal-management vendors while reducing direct water consumption.

researchConclusion: Do not treat all water stocks as one trade. The strongest current setup is a barbell: direct thermal infrastructure (MOD/VRT/TT) plus lower-beta water security/reuse (ECL/XYL/Veolia). The main risk is that data centres increasingly adopt waterless cooling where water infrastructure is constrained, which shifts value from water volume toward cooling efficiency, reuse technology and integrated resource management.
